reading.body:
The Weaver is an OpenStreetMap record tagged as a data center whose name gives no positive signal of any data-center business, so its identity and function remain unconfirmed.

The record carries a name that more commonly evokes textiles, craft, or a pub or creative business, none of which are typical data-center trades. That mismatch is the only evidence here, and it points toward a possibly misapplied tag rather than a verified facility. The entry records the uncertainty instead of resolving it.

For AI specifically, this matters only as a caution about the input layer. Capacity estimates built on facility counts inherit the accuracy of tags like this one, and a single mistagged node is a small error that compounds when aggregated. The record sits near Alicante-Elche airport, but proximity to an airport is not evidence of compute, power, or a building built for servers.

What the data does not cover is substantial. There is no operator, no website, no megawatt figure, no build date, and no confirmation either way. The research status is exhausted, meaning the question was left open rather than answered. Nothing here should be read as a data center, and nothing here should be read as proof that it is not.
